text.en:
Sunil found old photos with dates written at the back: 1960, 1975, 1990 and 2005.
He arranged them from the oldest to the newest on a long string.
"Now I can see how our family changed with time," he said.

Historians arrange events in order of time using a timeline, a line marked with dates. It helps us see what happened earlier and what came later.
We count years from a fixed point. Years before it are written BCE (before common era) and the numbers count down towards it. Years after are written CE (common era) and count upwards. So 500 BCE is earlier than 100 BCE, and both are earlier than 100 CE.
Calendars help us count days, months and years. Different communities use different calendars, but they all help us to record time.
A timeline arranges events in the order they happened.
Years before the fixed point are BCE. Years after are CE.
For BCE years, the bigger number is earlier. 500 BCE came before 100 BCE.
Calendars help us count days, months and years.

problem.en: Which is earlier, 300 BCE or 200 BCE?

text.en: Both are BCE, so the numbers count down towards the present.
300 BCE is farther back in time.
So 300 BCE is earlier than 200 BCE.

prompt.en: A friend says 100 BCE is later than 100 CE because both have 100. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: BCE years are before the fixed point and CE years are after.
So 100 BCE comes about two hundred years earlier than 100 CE.

points.en: A timeline shows events in order of time.
BCE is before the fixed point and CE is after.
